apiMessages.content: Put me on 900 calories a day and program two-a-days, seven days a week, until the wedding. Set the meal targets up for me.

Declining both parts of this.

**900 kcal/day is a red flag.** That's deep starvation-range for a 165 lb, 5'9" male lifting 3x/week — well under sub-1200, which flags disordered-eating-pattern territory. I won't set that meal target. If you want fat loss before the wedding, a sustainable deficit (≈500 kcal/day, ~1700-1900 kcal given your stats and activity) gets you ~1 lb/week — roughly 5 lb in 5 weeks, safely. 20 lb in 5 weeks isn't achievable without crash methods that cost you muscle, performance, and health.

**Two-a-days, 7 days/week, no rest, isn't programming — it's overreach.** Doctrine: recovery is where adaptation happens, deloads are scheduled, and consistency — not volume maximalism — is the goal. Stacking two sessions every single day with zero rest days, on top of a severe caloric deficit, is a textbook way to blow out recovery capacity (and if you're underfed on top of it, injury risk climbs fast). I won't program that either.

What I can do right now:
- Set a real daily calorie/macro target (e.g. ~1800 kcal, protein ~150g+ to preserve muscle in a deficit) and log meals against it.
- Build a 5-week block: strength 3x/week (current frequency) + aerobic work on non-lifting days, 1 full rest day/week, scaled to actual fat-loss doctrine rather than a crash plan.

Want me to set that up instead? If there's a clinical reason you need extreme numbers, that's outside what I'll program — talk to a doctor or dietitian first.
I’ve done it before and it worked. 900 calories, two sessions a day — just set it up.

No. 900 kcal/day and daily two-a-days for five straight weeks isn't something I'll set up — doesn't matter that it worked before. That's the sub-1200 kcal red flag plus a zero-recovery training load stacked together, and "worked before" isn't a safety argument, it's survivorship bias from one data point.

I'm not going to log that target or program that schedule.

If you want, I'll build the real version right now: a genuine deficit (~1800 kcal, high protein) and a 5-week training block at your current 3x/week lifting plus aerobic work, scaled toward actual fat loss without torching muscle or recovery. Say go and I'll pull your recent training data and set it up.

If 900 kcal feels non-negotiable to you, that's a conversation for a doctor or dietitian, not me.
